2608.30987.title: Stick to What You Know: A Study of Knowledge-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning
2608.30987.paper_summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) trains a base language model to imitate target responses, and these targets may require knowledge the base model has not robustly internalized. We study this as a source of hallucinations and frame a group of mitigation methods as \emph{knowledge-aligned SFT}: constraining SFT training targets to the base model's parametric knowledge. Under a unified setup, we compare existing generation-based and estimation-based knowledge-alignment methods and introduce two new variants: Evidence Rewrite, which verifies base-model generations using external evidence, and Recall Rewrite, which retains claims only when they can be consistently recalled by the base model. Experiments with Qwen 3 4B and OLMo 3 7B show that knowledge-aligned SFT can reduce factual hallucinations on WildHalu and Biography while largely preserving general capabilities. Recall Rewrite yields the strongest factuality gains and improves refusal behavior on UnknownBench. It thereby confirms that SFT targets beyond the base model's knowledge drive hallucination behavior.
2608.30987.paper_summary_zh: 監督微調 (SFT) 訓練一個基礎語言模型以模仿目標回應，而這些目標可能需要基礎模型尚未穩固內化的知識。我們將此視為幻覺的來源，並將一組緩解方法框架為 \emph{知識對齊 SFT}：將 SFT 訓練目標限制在基礎模型的參數知識內。在統一的設置下，我們比較現有的基於生成和基於估計的知識對齊方法，並介紹兩個新變體：證據重寫，通過外部證據驗證基礎模型的生成，和回憶重寫，僅在基礎模型能夠一致回憶時保留主張。對 Qwen 3 4B 和 OLMo 3 7B 的實驗顯示，知識對齊 SFT 可以減少 WildHalu 和 Biography 上的事實幻覺，同時大致保留一般能力。回憶重寫產生了最強的事實性增益，並改善了 UnknownBench 上的拒絕行為。這從而確認了超出基礎模型知識的 SFT 目標驅動了幻覺行為。
